newsitem.title: FINLAND: Analysts see markka allowed in 2.96-3.11/DM range.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see markka allowed in 2.96-3.11/DM range.

text.p: The Finnish markka is expected to be allowed to trade in a range of 2.96-3.11 per German mark without central bank intervention, according to a Reuters poll.

The markka joined Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) on October 14 at a central parity exchange rate of 3.04 markka per mark. The official fluctuation band in the ERM is 15 percent either side of the midpoint, or 2.62-3.53 for DEM/FIM.
If DEM/FIM moves 2.25 percent up or down from 3.04, the band would be 2.97-3.11. The poll tried to gauge where market players expect the Bank of Finland to intervene.
For the lower limit, the mean of the forecasts by 22 dealers, analysts and economists was at 2.96 in a 2.82-3.01 range.
Almost three quarters (16 of 22 respondents) put the lower limit between 2.93 and 2.98, while three saw it below 2.93. Three operators expected it to be above 2.98.

For the upper limit, the mean of the forecasts was 3.11 and they ranged from 3.05 to 3.25. Slightly more than half (12) the forecasts were in a 3.09-3.11 range, six were above 3.11 and four were below 3.09. @
When the markka was linked to the ERM, Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen said the markka will not be forced into any secretly pre-defined narrower band inside the broad fluctuation limits.
It was also, however, clear that the definition of exchange rate stability in ERM was not plus-minus 15 percent, and it was also quite obvious that it was not 2-1/4 percent up or down, she said.
Before joining the ERM, the markka floated slightly more than four years.
The poll was carried out on Thursday last week. Forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis.

Forecasts by: Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd., Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), Enso, Handelsbanken Markets Finland, Helaba Landesbank (Frankfurt am Main), Huhtamaki Finance, Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, S-E Banken (Helsinki), SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
